routes.label: Consider the two possible sign patterns

question: Suppose \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are nonzero real numbers, and \(a+b+c=0.\) What are the possible value(s) for \[\dfrac{a}{|a|}+\dfrac{b}{|b|}+\dfrac{c}{|c|}+\dfrac{abc}{|abc|}?\]
solution:
For any nonzero real number \(x\), the quotient \(x/|x|\) equals \(1\) if \(x>0\) and \(-1\) if \(x<0\). Thus only the signs of \(a,b,c\) matter. All denominators are positive because the numbers and their product are nonzero.

Since \(a+b+c=0\), the three numbers cannot all be positive or all be negative. There are exactly two possibilities:

If two numbers are positive and one is negative, the first three quotients sum to \(1+1-1=1\). The product \(abc\) is negative, so the full expression is \(1-1=0\).

If one number is positive and two are negative, the first three quotients sum to \(1-1-1=-1\). The product \(abc\) is positive, so the full expression is \(-1+1=0\).

These cases cover every allowed triple, and allowed triples exist, such as \((1,1,-2)\). Therefore the only possible value is \(\boxed{0}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
